635844c8c6852770.description: As a Database Administrator, you ll take ownership of the health and operational reliability of our production databases. You ll also work closely with engineering, cloud, and reliability teams to help developers make better database decisions, prevent production incidents, and improve the way database changes are designed and delivered. Optimize queries, indexing, and database resource utilization. Manage backups, point-in-time recovery, and disaster recovery. Implement database replication, high availability, and failover strategies. Plan database upgrades, migrations, and safe schema changes. Maintain database security, access controls, and auditing. Automate database operations using Bash, Python, or similar tools. Troubleshoot database incidents and perform root-cause analysis. Collaborate with engineering, DevOps, SRE, and Cloud teams to improve database reliability and scalability. You ve identified the most significant risks and improvement opportunities across availability, performance, backup, and recovery. By day 60: You re independently handling assigned database administration and troubleshooting activities. You ve reviewed backup configurations and started validating recovery procedures for critical databases. You ve identified gaps in database monitoring and alerting, including replication lag, WAL contention, autovacuum, and table bloat. You re contributing to database performance improvements and operational documentation. By day 90: Critical database restore tests have been completed or are progressing against an agreed recovery-testing plan, with gaps documented and corrective actions defined. Key database failure scenarios are documented through practical runbooks. Database monitoring and alerting improvements have been implemented for prioritized operational risks. You re actively contributing to database reliability, performance, and incident-prevention initiatives. By day 120: A safer database change-management process is in place, including appropriate reviews, DDL auditing, and rollback planning. A practical PostgreSQL major-upgrade roadmap has been developed, with compatibility and migration risks assessed. The high-availability approach for the SITE database environment has been evaluated and documented. Database size and activity metrics are available to support the per-customer cost-allocation initiative. Familiarity with database observability, capacity planning, and per-customer database usage or cost allocation. Experience working in SaaS, data-platform, fintech, banking, or telecommunications environments. Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools and automated database provisioning. Relevant certifications, such as EDB PostgreSQL or AWS certifications. What the hiring process will look like Mawhub screening Technical screen (45 min) [DB Lead] Technical deep-dive (60 90 min) with a practical scenario: diagnosing replication lag and WAL contention, planning a zero-downtime major upgrade [DB Lead + SRE Team Lead] Hiring manager interview Mahmoud Moharam, Cloud Manager Culture fit interview - HR Director Desired Candidate Profile Who You Are You re an experienced Database Administrator who understands that managing production databases is about more than keeping services running. You know how to prevent data loss, diagnose complex performance problems, plan high-risk changes, and build systems that remain reliable under pressure. You re comfortable working with large, business-critical databases and can balance operational stability with the need to improve architecture, automation, and scalability. Technically, you likely: Have 5+ years of hands-on PostgreSQL administration experience in production. Have experience with AWS Aurora, Amazon RDS, MySQL, and self-managed Linux databases. Understand database performance tuning, replication, high availability, and disaster recovery. Have experience managing multi-terabyte databases, upgrades, and migrations. Can automate database operations using Bash or Python. When it comes to database resilience: You have hands-on experience with backups, recovery, replication, and failover. You can troubleshoot database incidents and minimize downtime. You follow safe change-management practices and maintain rollback plans. When it comes to database performance: You can troubleshoot slow queries, indexing, locking, and resource utilization. You understand PostgreSQL internals and multi-tenant database challenges. You document your work and continuously improve database reliability.
